name: CA-39
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Mark Takano running in a D+7 district
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Takano holds a D+7 seat with incumbency and a large fundraising edge, while Manos shows no reported cash. Markets price the race at 98% Democratic, matching fundamentals pointing to a roughly 20-point margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Takano would be the first sign of a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark Takano, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Riverside-area district that leans Democratic by about seven points. He advanced to the general election and has raised nearly $900,000, while Republican Steve Manos has no reported fundraising and little outside support. No independent groups are spending against Takano.

With no public general-election polling in the race, the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap, all of which favor Takano by a wide margin. Prediction markets price his chances at about 98 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling rather than any specific evidence of a competitive contest.
